why: An epoch is a startable world: clock, gases, ice, sea level, an optional landscape archetype, and a palette hint. Palaeogeography uses the existing land archetypes; it does not reconstruct plates. Venus-with-ocean and early Mars are first-cut and tagged. LGM and Cretaceous climate are not proxy-calibrated this cut.

epochs.name: Present
epochs.why: Holocene calibration Earth. Gases, ice and sea level stay on the ruleset so the golden hash does not move.
epochs.tip: Holocene Earth. Clock stays in years; modern biosphere owns life.

epochs.name: From origin
epochs.why: Clock at CAI. Little land, a close Moon, reducing air from the deep-time Earth path. The run is a history, not a snapshot.
epochs.tip: Hadean start. Regenerates the world; Adaptive clock runs in Myr and slows toward now.

epochs.name: Hadean
epochs.why: Steam-rich air, almost no continents, a Moon still close. Snapshot of the magma-ocean aftermath, not a plate reconstruction.
epochs.tip: Hot, wet, almost no land. Tides from a closer Moon.

epochs.name: Archean
epochs.why: No free oxygen, a methane greenhouse, green-grey iron ocean. Microbial mats only — grass does not exist yet.
epochs.tip: Reducing air, faint young Sun, mats not forests.

epochs.name: Snowball
epochs.why: Cryogenian hard snowball as a startable world. Ice to the equator; volcanic CO2 is the way out. Not a GCM hysteresis test.
epochs.tip: White Earth. Push CO2 or albedo to break the ice.

epochs.name: Cambrian
epochs.why: Animals possible, oxygen well above Archean, still no land plants. Clock sits at 541 Ma BP, not 541 Myr after CAI.
epochs.tip: Start ~541 Ma. Animals possible; oxygen already high enough for that question.

epochs.name: Carboniferous
epochs.why: Thirty-five per cent oxygen and wet coal-swamp land. Nothing digesting lignin yet — grass is still in the future.
epochs.tip: High O2, swamps, no grass. Biology is rewriting the air.

epochs.name: Permian
epochs.why: One supercontinent via the Pangaea archetype — not reconstructed plates. End-Permian doorstep, stressed climate.
epochs.tip: Start ~252 Ma — continents assembled, climate stressed.

epochs.name: Cretaceous
epochs.why: Hothouse, no polar ice, higher seas, an inland-sea archetype standing in for epicontinental seaways. Not proxy-calibrated this cut.
epochs.tip: No ice, seas high, an interior seaway. The standard hothouse.

epochs.name: Last glacial
epochs.cite: EPICA / ice-core CO2 190 ppm; Clark LGM ice
epochs.why: Sea level down, ice to mid-latitudes, 190 ppm CO2. Well constrained and cheap. Ice extent is a latitude paint, not a flowline model.
epochs.tip: 21 ka. Ice to ~40°, Beringia-ish low seas.

epochs.name: 10 ka ago
epochs.why: Younger Dryas-ish. Deep-time machinery on, gases near Holocene, almost now.
epochs.tip: Younger Dryas-ish. Deep-time machinery on, but the clock is almost Holocene.

epochs.name: Venus now
epochs.why: Present Venus. No patch — the catalogue ruleset already is the dry runaway.
epochs.tip: The Venus you have: dry, thick CO2, no ocean.

epochs.name: Venus ocean
epochs.why: First-cut wet Venus: dichotomy highlands and a real ocean, thinner CO2. Habitable for maybe two billion years is an argument, not a result this model claims.
epochs.tip: Same body, different region of world space. An ocean on Venus.

epochs.name: Mars now
epochs.why: Present Mars. No patch — thin CO2 and the dichotomy stamp already describe the desert.
epochs.tip: The Mars you have: thin air, ice at the poles.

epochs.name: Early Mars
epochs.why: Thicker air, a possible northern ocean on the dichotomy, polar ice still there. Valley networks are not carved this cut — the map is the archetype plus water.
epochs.tip: Noachian-ish. More air, a lowland ocean, ice remaining.
